That does not match Varma's sleek hair in a side knot from his sheet and from the neighbouring panels 7.2 to 7.5.
decisions.correction: The plain white European-cut cotton coat from the previous page lies folded on the timber table between the two men, front and centre and well lit: clean, plain white, one column of plain undecorated brass buttons, the red waistcoat folded beneath it, no lace, braid or coloured facings. There is no unrolled map on the table top and no game pieces. Marthanda Varma stands at the head of the table with his head bowed and his eyes lowered to the coat, one hand resting near it, NOT looking at Nagoji. He has the sleek black hair of his sheet in a side knot above his LEFT ear (no loose curls), the red forehead mark, gold bead necklaces, bare chest, a cream mundu with a gold border and a clean cloth bandage on his left shoulder. Nagoji stands across the table, still and watching the coat or the king, NOT pointing or touching anything. He has a Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, a white mundu and shoulder cloth, bare arms, the silver chain of office, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a tiny gold ear stud. Keep the same war hall (timber pillars, laterite walls, brass lamps, the latticed window at night) empty of everyone else, with plain wall or roof timbers in the upper third for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Varma's pose, bandaged left shoulder, room and night window all work, but the coat is wrong. It has dark navy facings and cuffs edged in gold lace, which read as Dutch blue or the Goa officer's gilt-laced coat, the very coat this panel's dialogue says it is not. It is also smeared with brown stains that could read as dried blood. All of this breaks continuity with the clean, plain white coat with brass buttons and red waistcoat drawn in 5.2 and 7.3. The wall map at upper left also carries tiny letter-like scribbles (pseudo-text).
decisions.correction: Keep Varma exactly as drawn (bare-chested, gold bead necklaces, the clean cloth bandage over his LEFT shoulder, cream mundu with a gold border, left arm extended holding the coat up by its collar at arm's length, his gaze on it), and keep the same war hall and night window. Redraw the coat as the same coat shown on the earlier pages: a long, clean, brand-new plain WHITE cotton coat of European cut. It has one single column of plain undecorated round brass buttons and plain white turned-back cuffs, with a glimpse of the red waistcoat lining. It has NO blue, navy or dark facings or cuffs, NO gold or gilt lace, braid or piping, and NO stains, smudges, dirt or spots anywhere on it. The maps pinned to the walls show only plain unlettered lines, with no labels, letters or writing-like marks.

decisions.issues: v01 misses the beat: there is no coat; Nagoji's fingertip presses a brass counter on a map among game pieces. The reaching arm is his RIGHT arm, and the brand is on its outer forearm, not on the inner LEFT wrist. His face is sharp and in focus instead of out of focus. His hair hangs loose in curls with no Kerala topknot.
decisions.correction: Close insert at table height. The plain white European-cut coat (clean, plain white, no lace or coloured facings) lies on the timber table and fills the lower half of the frame, with one plain undecorated round brass button large and sharp in the foreground. There is no map, no counters and no game pieces. Nagoji's LEFT hand comes in from the left, turned on its edge with the thumb up so the INNER wrist faces the camera and shows the old pale puckered brand just above the wrist (no letters or numerals). His fingers have ridged nails and hover a finger's width ABOVE the button, clearly not touching it. Above and behind the hand, his face is soft and blurred out of focus: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, hair bound in a Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, white shoulder cloth, silver chain. Keep the warm brass-lamp light and dark timber background, with plain dark wall or shadow in the upper corner for one balloon.

decisions.issues: The object Varma sets down is a folded cream textile with heavy gold embroidered borders, which reads as a mundu or shawl, not the white European coat. The beat (the coat set down between them) is lost. Varma, his bandaged left shoulder and the room are otherwise fine.
decisions.correction: Keep Varma's pose, look and bandage and the same war hall at night. What his hand sets down on the timber table must be unmistakably the same coat as the earlier panels: a long, plain WHITE cotton coat of European cut, folded with one sleeve and a turned-back cuff visible, one column of plain undecorated round brass buttons catching the lamplight, and the red waistcoat showing beneath it. It has NO gold borders, NO embroidery and NO coloured facings, and must not look like a draped cloth or shawl. Place it on the near side of the table toward the viewer, as if set down for someone standing across from him, and leave the upper part of the frame (roof timbers and plain laterite wall) free for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Nagoji is wearing the white coat and red waistcoat. On page 8 he is not yet in uniform, the coat must lie on the table in front of him, and no one wears the coat in this room. His hair hangs loose in curls instead of a topknot. Varma at the window has grey at the temple; his hair should be black.
decisions.correction: Keep the wide strip composition and the same war hall: Varma standing at the latticed window at the right with his back to the room, night outside, and Nagoji alone at the table on the left. Nagoji must NOT wear the coat. He is in a white mundu and shoulder cloth with bare arms, the silver chain of office over his bare chest, his hair bound in a Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a tiny gold ear stud. The plain white European-cut coat (clean, plain white, one column of plain brass buttons, red waistcoat beneath, no lace or coloured facings) lies folded on the table in front of him, and he looks down at it with both hands resting on the table edge. Varma has black hair with no grey, in a side knot, and a clean cloth bandage at the back of his LEFT shoulder; he is bare-chested with gold necklaces and a cream mundu with a gold border. Leave the dark roof timbers and plain upper wall clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The small pennant is drawn as a straight blue saltire rather than a diagonal crossed by a curved line. It is drawn the same way in panels 2 to 4, so the page stays consistent. De Lannoy's head is turned to profile, a glance aside rather than strictly 'not turning', but his body stays at the parapet facing out. Nagoji's left-forearm scars show as two thin crossing pale lines instead of a puckered brand patch with one long scar. They are small at reading size. The drill men are bare-chested with staves, while in panel 2 they wear white tunics and carry muskets. The sea is more prominent than 'a distant line'. Otherwise correct: Nagoji climbs the last steps with his topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain, mundu and shoulder cloth, and no coat or knife. De Lannoy wears the patched, frayed white coat and holds a brass cup. The scene is a laterite bastion at sunset with copper drill ground below, and there is ample open sky in the top left and top centre for three balloons.

Minor only. The camera is over the shoulder and slightly high, not a true low angle along the parapet. The drill men wear white tunics with red sashes and carry muskets, and two instructors wear dark blue sleeveless vests. That differs from the bare-chested men with staves in panel 1, but they are small background figures. The pennant is a straight saltire (same as the rest of the page). The beat is clear: De Lannoy turns the brass cup in freckled pale hands, eyes on the drill below, sun low behind the far hills. His coat is patched and frayed and his hair is tied with a black ribbon. Open sky to the right of his head and across the top has room for two balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji's ear studs are small round gold balls on both lobes. They are still studs, nothing hangs from them. His topknot has a thin gold band. The pennant is a straight saltire (same as the rest of the page). The beat is clear: De Lannoy laughs softly with eyes lowered, cup raised near his mouth, and Nagoji leans on the parapet at his shoulder watching him. Nagoji's thick curled moustache, clean chin, grey temples, silver chain, shoulder cloth and bare arms all match. Clean sky across the top and to the right of Nagoji's head has room for three balloons. The hands are sound.

The only candidate, v01, inverts the script beat. The script says 'Lannoy turned to face Nagoji, the sunset behind him', with Nagoji off-panel in the viewer's place. Instead De Lannoy is seen from behind: back to the viewer, hands on the parapet, looking out at the sunset with his head turned aside to the right. That is essentially the panel 1 pose, so the turn toward Nagoji for this confession never happens and the sunset is in front of him, not behind. His head also sits in the top third of the strip (about 8 to 32 percent of the height), outside the required middle half. Costume, hair, bastion, standard and drill ground are otherwise good.
decisions.correction: De Lannoy has now turned his back on the parapet and the sea to face Nagoji, who stands off-panel exactly where the viewer is. Show De Lannoy from the front or three-quarter front, face and both eyes toward the viewer, expression rueful and serious. The low setting sun and copper sky must be directly BEHIND him, so his hair and shoulders are rim-lit and his face is in warm half-shadow. He is NOT seen from behind, NOT looking out over the parapet, and NOT looking off to the side. He may lean back against the laterite parapet, holding the brass cup loosely at his waist in one pale freckled hand. Keep his head and shoulders inside the middle half of the strip height (top of the head no higher than a quarter of the way down the frame), set left or right of centre so open, low-detail sky stays clear on the other side for two speech balloons. Keep everything that already works: the worn white Travancore coat with patched elbows and frayed cuffs, pale curly hair tied back with a black ribbon, bare-headed, the red laterite bastion with its banner staff and the drill ground below. Nagoji is not in the frame, and there is no text anywhere.

decisions.issues: Minor: the two figures are warmly lit rather than true silhouettes, and in this back view De Lannoy's elbow patch reads more like a ragged worn hole than the sewn patch of 10.1. The sun sits on the left here but on the right in 10.1, 10.4 and 10.5. Nagoji (topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin, stud, shoulder cloth, silver chain, no coat) and De Lannoy (pale tied hair, worn white coat, bare-headed) both match. The large sky at upper left is clear for the balloon.

v01 paints the brand as a crisp dark tattoo-like glyph (reads as a delta or Taurus symbol, i.e. a letter-like mark) on the BACK of the wrist of his near RIGHT arm. The bible wants a pale puckered scar on the INNER LEFT forearm, blurred past reading, with the long white scar beside it. The framing is also a mid shot of face and arm rather than the scripted close-up on the hand gripping the stone. His hair hangs loose under a small bun instead of the gathered Kerala topknot of 10.2 and 10.5, and there is stubble shading on the chin.
decisions.correction: Frame this as a true close-up of Nagoji's LEFT hand and forearm only, with his face out of frame (at most the edge of his jaw and the gold-bordered white shoulder cloth at the frame edge). The hand grips the top edge of the red laterite parapet with the forearm turned so the INNER, palm-side wrist and forearm face the camera, thumb uppermost, and the fingernails are visibly ridged. The old brand sits on that inner left forearm a hand's width above the wrist: a pale, puckered patch of raised scar ridges, lighter than the surrounding skin and blurred past reading. It is never a dark ink tattoo, symbol, glyph, letter, numeral or cross, and never on the back of the wrist or hand. A long, thin white scar runs from the wrist toward the elbow beside it. Show a bare forearm with no coat sleeve, bracelet or bandage. Keep the dusk light, the laterite stone texture and a soft view of the drill ground and the distant sea line behind, with clear, low-detail sky in the upper part of the frame for two balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 is otherwise strong and matches the beat and the rest of the page: Nagoji leans on the parapet looking toward the sea, with Kerala topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white mundu and gold-bordered shoulder cloth, and no coat. The fail is the oval silver medallion at the end of his chain of office: it is engraved with three rows of script-like pseudo-writing, which counts as painted pseudo-text.
decisions.correction: The silver chain of office must end in a plain, smooth, polished silver oval or disc with NO engraving, inscription, script-like lines, letters, numerals, seal or emblem on its face. Alternatively, let the heavy silver chain hang plain with no pendant. Keep everything else exactly as before. Nagoji stands at the left, leaning his folded forearms on the red laterite parapet, in profile facing right toward the sea. He has the Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a tiny flush gold ear stud, a white mundu and the gold-bordered white shoulder cloth, bare arms and no coat. Keep the angled bastion with the banner staff, the red standard with the silver conch and the white pennant with dark blue lines, and the red-dust drill ground below with men in white mundu. Keep the dusk sky, with the sun on the distant sea line at right, and leave the upper sky clear and low-detail for two short balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the frame cuts the officer at mid-nose rather than at the chin (his eyes are still never shown), and his coat and red waistcoat keep full colour inside the grey stain. Everything the script asks for is there: a pale clean-shaven jaw, a black tricorne, a queue with a black ribbon, the gilt-laced white coat with ornate gilt buttons, the red waistcoat, the smallsword and the hand drawing the cuff. The two guards wear morions, buff jerkins and off-white shirts, with nothing red or blue. The open cell shows empty manacles. There is no text, blood or noose. The plain grey cell wall at upper right (and the corridor vault at upper left) is clear space for the one off-panel balloon.

The officer's costume contradicts 11.1 and the script. Above the shoe hangs a black cloak or cape, and his cream coat skirt has a plain round button with no gilt lace. The ornate-versus-plain button contrast is a deliberate motif (14.3 mirrors it). The deep white cuff the script puts at the top of the frame is missing. The shoe is planted flat on the floor, not lifting carefully over the flagstones. The buckle, the guard, the wet floor and the cell with its manacles are good.
decisions.correction: The officer's coat must match 11.1 exactly. At the top of the frame show the deep turned-back white cuff of his coat sleeve, edged with gilt lace, with two ornate gilt buttons and a white lace ruffle, his pale hand hanging relaxed beside it. Below it show the white coat skirt edged with gilt lace. Draw no black cloak, cape, dark lining or other dark garment, and no plain buttons. The black buckled shoe is lifted in mid-step: the heel is clearly off the ground and the sole a hand's breadth above the wet flagstones as he steps carefully over a spot just out of frame, with a white stocking above it. Keep the ornate silver buckle, the floor-level camera and the grey, desaturated dawn light. Keep the single gaol guard waiting in the corridor behind (morion, buff jerkin, off-white shirt, dark breeches) and the open cell with empty manacles on a ring. Leave the plain grey wall at upper right clear for two balloons. Nothing at all lies on the floor.

decisions.issues: The script beat fails. The figure leaving through the door is a gaol guard (morion helmet, leather jerkin, dark breeches), not the officer's white back. The palette is warm and near-photographic instead of the grey, desaturated inked stain of 11.1 and 11.2. A heaped blanket on the cell floor could read as a body, against 'nothing on the floor is ever shown'. The low viewpoint from inside the cell and the empty manacles on a ring at the top edge are correct.
decisions.correction: The figure leaving through the door must be the Goa officer, not a gaol guard. Show him from behind as a pale European in a black tricorne, his hair tied in a queue with a black ribbon, in a long deep-cuffed white coat edged with gilt lace that hangs to the knee, with a smallsword hilt at his left hip, white stockings and black buckled shoes, walking away into the corridor. He wears no morion helmet, no leather jerkin and no puffed breeches. The heavy iron-bound cell door is swinging shut, already more than half closed, so his white back is framed in the narrowing gap. Render it in the same inked graphic-novel line and grey, desaturated dawn palette as the corridor panels, not warm and not photographic. Keep the low viewpoint from inside the cell, the empty iron manacles on a short chain hanging slack from a ring at the top edge, the wet flagstones and a plain upper wall clear for two balloons. The cell floor is bare stone with at most a little scattered straw: no blanket, no heap of cloth and no shape that could read as a body. Gaol guards may wait far down the corridor.

decisions.issues: Nagoji's ear ornament is a stud with a gold pearl drop hanging below it. The bible and the author's 2026-10-02 decision require a tiny flush stud with nothing hanging, enforced at selection. Lesser faults: his silver chain of office hangs with its medallion on his back at the shoulder blade, a thin gold band is tied round his topknot, De Lannoy's clasped hands are brown rather than pale and freckled, and the pennant shows a blue diagonal crossed by a brown bar or stick instead of a dark blue curved line. The composition, the dusk sky for lettering, De Lannoy's patched, fray-cuffed coat and pale tied hair, and Nagoji's moustache, clean chin, grey temples, mundu and shoulder cloth are all good.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud sitting on the lobe with nothing hanging from it: no pearl, bead or drop below it. His silver chain of office hangs around his neck to the front of his chest. Seen from behind, only the chain at the back of his neck shows; its pendant is out of sight on his chest and never hangs on his back or shoulder blade. His topknot is tied with plain cloth, with no gold band or ornament in the hair. De Lannoy's clasped hands are pale and freckled like his face, not brown. The pennant below the standard is white with one dark blue diagonal line crossed by one dark blue curved line, with no bar, stick or other object on it. Keep everything else as drawn. De Lannoy stands at left in his patched, fray-cuffed white coat, his pale hair tied with a black ribbon, his head turned toward Nagoji. Nagoji stands at the parapet looking out to the sea: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, white mundu with gold-bordered shoulder cloth, bare arms. Keep the laterite bastion, the red standard with the silver conch, and the dusk sky across the top, kept clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: The framing misses the script. It asks for a wide shot with the two men SMALL at the parapet. Here De Lannoy and Nagoji are large foreground figures filling the left half of the frame, so the panel nearly repeats 11.4's over-the-shoulder two-shot and loses the pull-back. The pennant is a straight blue X (a saltire) rather than a diagonal crossed by a curved line. The rest is good: the drummer, the bare-chested men in white mundu forming up with no coats, the brass oil lamps, Nagoji's flush ear stud, moustache and clean chin, De Lannoy's patched coat over a white mundu, and the sky for lettering.
decisions.correction: Pull the camera far back to a high wide shot over the drill ground at dusk. De Lannoy and Nagoji are SMALL figures at the bastion parapet, each no taller than about one fifth of the frame height, placed in the upper left third against the sky, so that the drill ground with the drummer and the forming ranks fills most of the frame. They must not be large foreground figures, and the shot must not repeat the over-the-shoulder two-shot of the previous panel. Keep them readable as silhouettes. De Lannoy is tall, in a white coat over a white mundu, his pale hair tied back. Nagoji wears a topknot, white mundu and shoulder cloth, bare arms and the silver chain, and no coat. Keep the drummer beating the evening call and the bare-chested men in white mundu with long muskets forming ranks, all without coats. Keep the brass oil lamps, the laterite bastion with the red standard bearing a silver conch, the setting sun on the distant sea line, and clear dusk sky across the top for two balloons. The pennant below the standard is white with one dark blue diagonal line crossed by one dark blue curved line, not a straight X cross.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the pennant is drawn as a blue saltire, not a diagonal line crossed by a curved line, but it matches every other panel on the page. Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny gold hug-the-lobe ring seen from behind, with nothing hanging, so it reads as a stud. Otherwise clean: an over-the-shoulder view of both men at the parapet. De Lannoy's white coat is patched at the elbows with frayed cuffs, and his pale hair is tied with a black ribbon. Nagoji has his topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin, mundu with shoulder cloth and a thin silver chain. The drill men below are bare-chested in white mundu, there is last light, and the upper sky is open for both balloons.

Minor only: there is faint stipple shading on the chin and jaw, which reads as skin texture, not a beard. The sky is bluer than in panel 1, and the same saltire pennant appears. Tiny training posts on the distant drill ground include a couple with crossbars, with no rope or noose. Nagoji matches: a flush gold ear stud, curled moustache, topknot, grey temple, silver chain of office with a conch pendant and no coat. He is turning toward frame right, where De Lannoy stands off-panel. There is ample sky above for three balloons.

Minor only: the tiny distant drill men wear white knee-length tunics with dark legs, not the bare-chested mundu of panel 1, but they are too small to read as uniform coats. A wooden hoisting frame at the lower right has no rope. The beat is clear: De Lannoy's freckled hand, with sound anatomy, sets a brass cup on the laterite parapet. His face above it is turned toward frame right, toward Nagoji. His coat is patched at the elbows with frayed cuffs, and his hair is tied with a black ribbon. Sky at the upper left, between his head and the flagpole, and at the far right leaves room for three balloons.

Minor only: the drill ground behind him is still lit gold rather than dim, and it is empty except for training posts and frames, with no noose. His body is square to camera and his head is turned to frame right toward Nagoji, with last light on one side of his face. He matches his sheet: worn white coat with a patched elbow and frayed cuffs, sound freckled hands, bare head and ribbon-tied pale hair. The sky at the upper left and centre fits two balloons.

The only candidate, v01, breaks the author's ear-stud rule from 2026-10-02, which is to be enforced at selection. Nagoji's earlobe carries a small white stud with a round gold ball hanging below it, which is the drop from the sheet. In this full-width face panel it is clearly visible. Smaller issues: light stubble shading on the chin and jaw, and the topknot almost touches the top edge. Otherwise the composition, light, costume, brass oil lamp and open sky for lettering are good.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, light and costume. That means the wide strip with Nagoji at the left in three-quarter view, gazing out toward the setting sun with his jaw set. Keep the Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, the bare shoulders, the white mundu and the shoulder cloth with its gold-and-green border. Keep the heavy silver chain of office, the brass oil lamp and conch standard on the bastion behind him, and the open evening sky on the right for lettering. Fix the ear: on his visible earlobe draw ONLY one tiny round gold stud, no bigger than a lentil, sitting flat and flush on the lobe. Draw no gold ball, bead, pearl, drop or ring hanging beneath the lobe, no second white gem or stone, and nothing dangling from the ear at all. Keep his chin and jaw smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble shading. Lower his head slightly so the topknot clears the top edge and his face sits within the middle half of the strip's height.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the white pennant is drawn as a straight blue saltire rather than one diagonal plus one curved line (small, no lettering); Nagoji's shoulder cloth has a red border here but a gold border in 13.2 and 13.3. De Lannoy matches his sheet (pale hair tied with a black ribbon, worn white coat with elbow patches, fingering a frayed cuff, rueful downward look). Nagoji: thick curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, mundu, shoulder cloth, silver chain, no coat, scar on the inner left forearm. Open sky upper left and upper centre for both balloons.

Minor: the lamps along the wall are already lit, with nobody shown lighting them. The shoulder cloth border is gold, but red in 13.1. The pennant is the same saltire as in 13.1. Otherwise clean: it is a wide shot over the two men at the parapet, and on the drill ground a bare-chested recruit in a white mundu fumbles his musket while an officer points and shouts. De Lannoy wears his patched and frayed white coat and is bare-headed. Nagoji is in profile with a clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot and silver chain. Dusk light. Large open sky across the top for both balloons.

Minor: the topknot reads only as hair piled on the crown from this angle. The lamplight on his cheek is subtle. Light stubble shading on the chin, but no beard. Nagoji's lit face dominates: thick curled moustache, flush gold stud, grey temples, silver chain, gold-bordered shoulder cloth, no coat, no knife, no bandage. A soft-edged grey stain of Keshavrao sits at the upper left edge and matches his sheet (hacked short black hair, faint moustache, torn grey-brown tunic). Open sky top centre and upper right for the caption and the short Nagoji balloon. A clay lamp on the parapet.

v01 puts Nagoji in the uniform: white coat, red waistcoat and brass buttons over a white mundu. 14.1 is the same night on the parapet as page 13, and the coats arrive 'a week later' in 14.2, which says he wears the uniform 'for the first time'. CONTINUITY row 24 @1-14.1 and the panel prompt both say: no coat, mundu and shoulder cloth, bare arms. Pages 13.1 and 13.3 draw him bare-chested in the mundu, so this frame breaks the sequence. Lesser problems: the pennant is an X of two straight lines rather than one diagonal crossed by a curved line, and there are tents on the drill ground below. Everything else works: De Lannoy's face, his patched and frayed coat, the night lamplight, the bastion, Nagoji's face, and the open sky for the balloons.
decisions.correction: Nagoji is NOT yet in uniform in this panel. It is the same night on the parapet as the previous page, a week before the coats arrive. Draw him exactly as on page 13: bare-chested with bare arms, in a white Kerala mundu with a white shoulder cloth with a thin red border over his left shoulder, the silver chain of office lying on his bare chest, Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold ear stud. He has NO white coat, NO red waistcoat, NO buttons and no sash. Keep everything else from the previous attempt: the starry night sky, clay lamps with open wicks on the laterite parapet, De Lannoy on the left in his worn white coat with the elbow patch and frayed cuffs, pale hair tied back with a black ribbon, the two men facing each other with De Lannoy giving one small sober nod and Nagoji's hands behind his back, and the open night sky across the upper third for the balloons. Under the red conch standard, the pennant is white with ONE straight dark blue diagonal line crossed by ONE curved dark blue line, never an X of two straight lines. No tents on the drill ground below.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. The reflection in the bronze mirror shows the hair loose with no topknot visible from the front, and it adds a white neckcloth. The reflection is posed frontally, which a cheat on mirror angle. The window is barred rather than shuttered, and there is light stubble shading on the jaw, but the chin reads clean. Everything required is here: white coat, red waistcoat, plain brass buttons, silver chain worn over the coat, white breeches, buckled riding boots, topknot with grey at the temples, gold stud, and a bare lime-washed room with the rolled mat, peg and bronze mirror. The two captions can go in the top-left corner above the window and on the plain wall below the mirror.

The shot is wider than 'tight on his hands': it is a waist-up shot with his face included. Still, the beat reads clearly: a brown hand drawing a white cuff straight with two fingers, and plain brass buttons on the cuff. The small wall mirror looks like aged glass rather than bronze, and the window has open shutters where 14.2 has bars. These are minor. Face is on model: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey temple, topknot. Hands are anatomically sound. The plain wall at upper right between the head and the mirror takes the caption.

In v01 the whole troop is already mounted. That contradicts Nagoji's line 'Mount up' and panel 14.5, where the troop swings into the saddle. Nagoji also wears a broad red sash wrapped over the waistcoat, which the script forbids ('no sash'). His sword is a straight short sword with a ball pommel, not a talwar. The ear ornament reads as a small hanging drop. What works: his face, topknot and grey temples, the chain over the coat, the boots, the rider muttering behind his hand, the startled young rider at right, the drill-ground setting, the red conch standard, and the open sky for the balloons.
decisions.correction: The troop is NOT yet mounted: Nagoji's next words are 'Mount up' and the following panel shows them swinging into the saddle. Draw the Maravar riders on foot, standing at their horses' heads or beside the saddles with the reins in hand. They wear white cotton coats with leather crossbelts and red waist sashes, some in red turbans and some bare-headed with topknots, all turning to stare at Nagoji. One in the middle ground mutters behind his hand to another. One young, beardless horseman near the right has his laugh dying on his face as he meets Nagoji's eyes. Nagoji himself wears NO sash and NO red waist cloth. His white coat hangs open over the red waistcoat with plain brass buttons and the silver chain of office lies over the coat. A plain narrow brown leather sword belt carries a CURVED talwar with a disc-pommel hilt in a curved scabbard, not a straight sword. He wears white knee breeches and tall black buckled riding boots, and his ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging from it. Keep from the previous attempt: Nagoji striding toward the camera in the centre, topknot with grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, eyes turned to the young horseman. Also keep the red-dust drill ground, laterite wall and angled bastion, the wooden targets and field gun, the single red conch standard, and the clear blue sky across the upper part for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. Nagoji is centred among the troop rather than clearly out in front. His ear ornament is a slightly rounded gold bead, small enough to pass. The troopers wear loose white jackets rather than tailored coats. Kayal's lower legs are cropped by the frame bottom, but the visible coat is bay with a black mane and no white markings, which matches the sheet. Nagoji is on model: coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, plain belt with no sash, boots, topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin. The troop is swinging into the saddle, the frame is the full-width 3:1 strip, and the red conch standard is the only flag. The open sky at upper left takes the caption.

v01 draws Father Duarte twice: once on the mule in the gateway, and again on foot in the foreground beside Nagoji with his face fully shown. That breaks the no-doubles rule and the script's instruction to hide the priest's face until panel 15.4. The mounted figure's face is also readable under the hat. The musketeers wear tricorne hats, but the troops on page 14 and in panels 15.2 and 15.3 are bareheaded with topknots. The pedimented gate also differs from the arched laterite gate in 15.2 and 15.4. Nagoji is correct: curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and chain.
decisions.correction: Draw Father Duarte exactly ONCE, only as a small, distant thin figure in black riding a long-eared mule just inside the gateway, with his head bowed and his face completely hidden in the shadow of his broad-brimmed black travel hat (no readable features). There is NO priest or cassocked figure on foot anywhere in the panel, and nobody in black stands near Nagoji. Around the mule, small at the gate: three men in dark plain coats and breeches (not cassocks), and a secretary with a record book under his arm. No soldiers escort them. Keep Nagoji exactly as in the previous attempt, alone in the right foreground: same face and profile, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny gold ear stud, grey at the temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. The drilling musketeers wear white coats with red sashes and crossed belts and are BAREHEADED with Kerala topknots. No tricorne or any other hat. The gate is an arched red-laterite gateway with small turrets, matching the rest of the page. Keep the upper third of the sky open and plain for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. Ramayyan stands at Nagoji's elbow facing him, not half turned toward the palace. Nagoji's chin has light stipple shading that reads as skin texture, not a beard. The arched laterite gate does not match panel 1 v01, which is being regenerated. Both characters match their sheets: Ramayyan's receding curly hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus; Nagoji's moustache, gold stud, grey temples, topknot, coat, waistcoat and chain. The troops are bareheaded with topknots, consistent with page 14. Lettering fits in the sky band at top left and top right.

Minor issues only. The gate and walls are a greyer stone than the red laterite in 15.2 and 15.4. Nagoji's expression reads as a wary sideways look more than a stunned stop. There is faint stipple texture on his chin, not a beard. He is mid-turn, looking back over his shoulder toward the stables, which fits the beat. Identity and uniform are correct: curled moustache, tiny gold stud, grey temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and chain. The troops are bareheaded with topknots, as in 15.2. The panel has no lettering.

Acceptable, with three points to note. (1) The animal a groom holds beside Duarte is a horse, not the mule from the script. (2) The background musketeers wear tricorne hats, while the troops in 15.2, 15.3 and on page 14 are bareheaded with topknots. (3) Duarte has already dismounted, holds his hat, and looks down while his secretary speaks to him, rather than talking to the secretary himself. Duarte matches the sheet and the older, greyer row for chapters 24 to 25: grey swept-back curls, lined face, stoop, ink-stained fingers, plain black cassock with a standing collar and a small cross, no collar tab. His right hand is tucked into the front of the cassock. The stables are across the yard behind him. There is no text, and the hands are sound. The open sky at the top centre takes the short caption.

v01 (only candidate): the three ropes hanging from the iron ring in the vault end in tied loops with wrapped knots. They read clearly as nooses, which the art rules and the setting both forbid. Duarte is also meant to be more than a decade younger with dark hair and no grey, but his hair is streaked with grey and his face is as deeply lined as his present-day self. The rest works: the red-lit vaulted chamber, the brazier, the empty stool, the plain table, the soft red stain edge, the bowed weary nod, the ink-stained clasped hands, the black cassock with a standing collar and small cross (no collar tab), and dark vault space at the upper left for the captions.
decisions.correction: Keep the red-lit vaulted stone chamber, the brazier on the far side, the empty stool and plain table in shadow, the soft-edged red stain border, and Duarte's pose: head bowed in a weary nod, ink-stained hands clasped low, plain black cassock with a plain standing collar and a small cross on a thin chain. Change the iron ring in the vault so that it holds only an empty iron ring, or at most one or two short, straight, plain rope ends with frayed cut tips hanging slack. There must be NO loops, NO knotted loops, NO coiled knots and nothing shaped like a noose anywhere in the frame. Make Duarte visibly about forty, more than a decade younger than his present self: hair entirely dark brown-black with not a single grey or silver strand, a smoother face with only faint lines, still thin and gaunt with a scholar's stoop. Keep the upper-left vault in deep, plain shadow for two captions.

decisions.issues: Minor: the low angle takes in more of the yard than a strictly tight shot would, and the trousers read as full-length ones tucked into the boots rather than clearly as knee breeches. The gate flies a plain white flag instead of the red conch standard, which matches 16.3. Otherwise clean: buckled brown riding boots mid-stride on packed red earth, the white coat's hem swinging above them, the red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain, drilling men in white coats with topknots, a field gun, the gate and stables. There is no text, and the upper-right sky is clear for the caption.

Clean three-slice composite. The same older, grey-haired Duarte appears in each slice, moving from a polite half-smile to confusion to wide-eyed recognition. He wears a black cassock with a standing collar and small cross, with no collar tab. The setting matches the parade ground, stables, gate and gun. Some background drill men wear black tricornes, as they also do in 15.1, 15.4 and 17.1. Space for the short caption is limited to the sky and flag area at the top of the first slice, to the right of the head (about x 0.24 to 0.33, y 0.0 to 0.2), or the sky at the upper left of slice 2. That space is adequate.

Minor: the script has the right hand twitching inside its sleeve, but here the ink-stained hand rests outside, over the other sleeve. The hands are still low and the pose is uneasy, so the beat survives. Full face, frightened, older and grey-haired, with the standing collar, small cross and no tab, matching his look on page 15. The background drill men wear black tricornes, consistent with the neighbouring pages. Open sky to the left of the head suits Duarte's short balloon, and the upper-right sky suits Nagoji's off-panel balloon, with its tail pointing to the right edge where Duarte is looking.

Clean. The shot is over Duarte's shoulder (grey hair, black cassock with standing collar) toward Nagoji. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a topknot, first grey at the temples and a small gold stud. The stud is a small round bead with nothing hanging from it. He wears the white coat with plain brass buttons, the red waistcoat, the silver chain over the coat and a sword hilt at the hip. Its knuckle-guard hilt matches 15.1. The drilling topknotted men in white coats are behind him, with a gun, the gate and the stables. The strip is wide (3:1) and the sky between the two heads and across the upper right is clear for the caption.

Minor: Duarte's ink-stained right hand already rests on his chest below the cross, which slightly anticipates the 17.3 gesture. The secretary has short curly hair here, where 15.4 shows hair tied back; he keeps the brown coat and the record book, so he still reads as the same man. Duarte matches his sheet: older and greyer, plain black cassock, standing collar, small cross, no collar tab. No painted text. The laterite wall and the sky at upper right are clear for the balloon.

Framing is a profile two-shot of the two men facing each other, not the scripted over-the-shoulder view past Duarte's grey head onto Nagoji. It still plays the beat: Nagoji answers level, in uniform, with the silver chain over the white coat. 16.5 already used the over-the-shoulder view, so the two-shot also adds variety. Nagoji matches: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold-set flush ear stud, topknot, grey at the temples, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons. His talwar is not visible. The fort wall here is greyer than the red laterite in the neighbouring panels, and the background soldiers are bareheaded instead of in tricornes. Both differences are minor. Clear sky between and above the heads for the two short balloons.

Minor: Duarte's fingertips reach the chain right beside the cross instead of clearly stopping short of it, but the hand plainly reads as rising to the cross and not grasping it. The hand anatomy is sound and the ink stains are on the hand. Same parade ground: stables, trough, gate and field gun. Open sky at upper left and upper right holds both balloons. Nagoji is off-panel to the right, where he stood in 17.2.

Minor: the angle is only modestly low, and his downcast expression reads reflective more than steadier. Both hands are hidden inside his sleeves at the waist, as scripted. Costume is correct, there is no painted text, and the setting matches. Large clear sky at upper right and upper left holds the two medium balloons.

Clean. A wide strip shows the white-coated lines at drill, the laterite star-fort walls with bastions, a field gun on its carriage, the gate, and the stables with a trough. No principals appear. The gate pediment carries only blank carved cartouches, with no lettering. A broad clear sky band across the top holds both balloons. Both speakers are off-panel, Duarte on the left and Nagoji on the right as in 17.2.

v01 is a handsome wide establishing shot (laterite walls and gate, tiled stables, horses drinking at the stone trough, field gun, white-coated squads), and Duarte (plain black standing collar, cross, ink-stained hands) and Nagoji (topknot, moustache, clean chin, stud, chain over the white coat) are both on-model. But the script beat is incomplete: the secretary hovering at a distance, unsure whether to intervene, is not drawn anywhere. He is established in 17.1 as a young curly-haired clerk in a brown robe-coat clutching a leather record book. The 'officer shouting commands' at the right is also a near-twin of Nagoji: the same white coat and red waistcoat, a thick moustache and long curly black hair. He reads as a second Nagoji in the same panel. And the two men are large mid-ground figures, not 'small in the middle of the fort's business'.
decisions.correction: Fix these points and keep everything else. 1) Add Father Duarte's secretary, the only other civilian in the yard: a young, slim Goan clerk with short curly black hair, clean-shaven, in a plain brown ankle-length coat-robe with a brown cloth sash. He clutches a closed brown leather record book to his chest with both arms. He stands alone on open red earth about ten paces behind the two men, half-turned toward them, one foot forward as if about to step in and then stopping. He must be clearly visible and not hidden by horses or soldiers. 2) The officer shouting commands must not look like Nagoji. Make him an older, heavier man with a short clipped grey moustache and short cropped hair under a plain white cloth cap. He wears a plain white coat with a red sash, no red waistcoat and no silver chain, his mouth open and his arm pointing toward the drilling squad. 3) Draw Duarte and Nagoji smaller, about two fifths of the frame height, walking side by side in the middle distance so the fort's business surrounds them. Keep what worked: the laterite star-fort walls and arched gate, the palms, the tiled-roof stables with horses, grooms watering horses at the long stone trough on the left, the field gun, the white-coated squads with muskets, and dry-season daylight on red earth. Keep Duarte in his plain black cassock with a plain black standing collar (no white at the throat) and a small cross on a thin chain. Keep Nagoji in the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain, with the Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and tiny gold ear stud.

decisions.issues: Clean. Nagoji stands close beside the downcast Duarte. Nagoji is on-model: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain. Duarte has a plain black standing collar with no tab, a cross and inked fingers. The same parade ground, gate, stables and trough as the rest of the page. Wide clear sky across the top for both Nagoji balloons.

Minor, not disqualifying. The background gate is drawn in dark grey stone with a small saint statue in a niche, unlike the red laterite gate in 18.1, 18.2 and 18.4. The drilling squad wears tricorns, which is consistent with the page 17 backgrounds. Duarte is on-model: grey swept hair, lined face, plain black standing collar with no tab, cross. His jaw is set and his eyes look right toward the off-panel Nagoji, as the beat requires. Clear sky across the top for both short balloons; Nagoji's line comes from off the right edge.

v01 fits the beat: a 3:1 strip with both faces in the middle band, Duarte at left facing Nagoji in profile at right, neither speaking, against the same parade ground, gun and stables. But Duarte shows a white Roman collar tab, a white notch of linen visible in the front gap of his standing collar at the throat. The bible and prompt explicitly forbid it as a 19th-century anachronism, and panels 18.1 to 18.3 all show a plain black collar. Nagoji's chin also carries some stubble hatching.
decisions.correction: Father Duarte's collar must be a plain black standing collar closed right round his throat in the same black cloth as the cassock. No white may show anywhere at his neck: no white tab, no white notch or gap at the front of the collar, no white band and no white linen. Nagoji's chin and jaw are smooth and fully clean-shaven, with no stubble shading. Keep everything else that worked: the 3:1 strip, with Duarte on the left in three-quarter view facing right and Nagoji on the right in left profile facing him. Both faces stay in the middle band of the height, neither speaking. Keep Duarte's grey swept hair, lined face and cross on a thin gold chain. Keep Nagoji's topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, tiny flush gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Keep the laterite fort walls and gate, the white-coated squads drilling, the field gun and the tiled stables with horses behind them, in dry-season daylight.

decisions.issues: Acceptable with small notes. The framing is a waist-up medium shot rather than truly tight, though Nagoji is alone with Duarte out of frame as scripted. He gazes off to the upper right rather than toward Duarte's side. A brass sword hilt shows at his hip. The gate is grey-brown stone with a faint niche figure, unlike the laterite gate in 18.1 and 18.2. There is light hatching texture on the chin, but no beard. He is otherwise on-model: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, tiny gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain. Open sky at the top right for both short balloons.

Clean. Duarte back of grey head and black shoulder in foreground, Nagoji beyond in white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons, silver chain over coat, topknot, grey at temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small flush gold stud. Parade ground, gate, field gun, stables and trough match neighbouring panels. The head shake is implied only by the bowed head. Balloon space in the open sky between the two heads.

Minor: Duarte's ink-stained gripping hand is drawn heavily wrinkled, older-looking than the 'more than a decade younger' brief, though only the hand shows. His chest and small cross appear at the top-left edge, but there is still only one cassock sleeve. The ropes hang from the iron ring in open loops with no noose knots. João's ruddy forearm, rolled cream sleeve, leather jerkin and key ring are correct, and the brazier glows red. No faces. The upper vault wall gives space for the off-panel balloon.

In this remembered Goa scene Duarte's hair is clearly salt-and-pepper grey and his face is deeply lined, so he reads as the same age as the present-day priest. That breaks the MUST MATCH line (in the page 19 stains he is more than a decade younger, hair still dark with no grey) and does not match the dark-haired younger Duarte chosen for the page 16 stain. Everything else works: the whitewashed courtyard burned to white at soft edges, the broad brown travel hat, the black cassock with standing collar and small cross, the ink-stained hand at the forehead, the chained prisoners in grey, brown and ochre rags seen from behind, and the buff-coated musketeers in broad hats with nothing red or blue, plus open sky for the balloons.
decisions.correction: Duarte in this remembered scene must be unmistakably more than a decade younger than the grey present-day priest: his hair is dark brown to near-black with NO grey or silver strands anywhere (as dark as the younger Duarte of the page 16 stain), and his face is leaner and smoother, with only faint lines and no deep furrows. Keep everything else as drawn: the glaring whitewashed Goa courtyard burned almost to white with soft edges, the gate on the far side, the broad round brown travel hat, the plain black cassock with plain standing collar and small cross on a thin chain, no white collar tab, and his ink-stained right hand with fingers held together touching his forehead to begin a slow, deliberate sign of the cross. His face and body turn toward the chain of prisoners in grey, brown and ochre rags, seen from behind with no recognisable faces. Buff-coated Portuguese musketeers in broad hats with matchlocks line the walls, with nothing red or blue, and the upper sky stays clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor: the gate pediment carries a small cross finial, and there is a tiny pale grey sliver at the front of the standing collar, which reads as shadow and not as a white tab. He wipes a tear with his ink-stained hand rather than only blinking, which still reads as the beat. The grey hair, lined face, cassock, small cross, parade ground, tricorn white-coat squads, field gun, stables and trough are all consistent with pages 17 to 19. The panel has no lettering.

Clean. Older grey Duarte, downcast, with a plain black standing collar (no white tab), small cross on a chain and ink-stained hands clasped and anatomically sound, on the same parade ground with gate, field gun, white-coat squads, stables and trough. The plain white flag has no marks. The wide open sky upper right holds both balloons.

v01 (the only candidate) draws Keshavrao as a full present-day figure in rags, standing beside Nagoji on the parade ground. The MUST MATCH line says he appears only in stains and never in the present, and the memory bleed calls for just a hand, with no face or figure. The stain itself (black water with a hand and a rope, upper right) and the setting (gate, field gun, stables, trough, dry daylight) are correct. Nagoji's uniform, topknot, grey temples and moustache are also correct. Minor: Nagoji has a sword hilt at his hip, while panels 20.2, 20.4 and 20.5 show none.
decisions.correction: Draw Nagoji ALONE as the only person in the present-day foreground. Do NOT draw Keshavrao as a standing or visible person anywhere in the frame: no young man in rags, no face, no body. Keshavrao exists only inside the memory stain: a faint, dark, smoky patch of black storm water behind Nagoji's shoulder on the right side. In it, one thin young hand and narrow wrist is losing its grip on the frayed end of a straight rope (no loop) and slipping into the waves. Keep Nagoji exactly as before: white coat, red waistcoat, plain brass buttons, silver chain over the coat, Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin. On his ear, only a tiny round gold stud flush on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. No sword or knife at his hip. Keep the same parade ground, gate, field gun, drilling squads, tiled stables and trough in dry daylight. Leave the upper-left sky clear and low in detail for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) gets the beat right: Nagoji striding toward the viewer across the parade ground, with the chain, brass buttons, red waistcoat, topknot and grey temples. The brand and scar show on his left forearm, there is plenty of upper-right sky for three balloons, and the setting is correct. But his ear ornament is a stud with a gold drop hanging below it. That breaks the MUST MATCH line (tiny flush gold stud, nothing hanging from it) and the author's ear = stud decision.
decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament must be ONLY a tiny round gold stud pressed flush against the earlobe, with NOTHING hanging below it: no drop, no bead, no pendant, no hoop. Do not copy the hanging drop from the reference sheet. Keep everything else exactly as in the previous attempt. Nagoji strides toward the viewer, slightly left of centre, in the white coat with sleeves turned back, plain brass buttons, red waistcoat and the silver chain of office over the coat. He has a Kerala topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin, and the brand with the long white scar on his left forearm. Keep the same parade ground, gate, drilling squads, field gun, tiled stables and trough. Leave a wide clear band of open sky across the upper right for three speech balloons.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) shows Duarte older and grey, bowed in a slow nod, with the cross on a chain and good open sky for balloons. But a pale cream sliver shows in the opening of his standing collar under the chin, which reads as a white Roman collar tab. That is the 19th-century anachronism the bible forbids. Minor: the background drill squads wear tricorn hats, while 20.2, 20.4 and 20.5 show bareheaded topknotted soldiers.
decisions.correction: Father Duarte's plain black standing collar is closed right up under his chin with no gap: no white, cream or linen visible at the collar opening, no Roman collar tab, no shirt or undershirt showing. The cassock is solid black from neck to hem, with only the small gold cross on its thin chain against it. Keep the rest of the previous attempt: Duarte older and greyer, gaunt and lined, grey hair swept back with loose curls, head bowed in a slow nod with eyes lowered, in the left half of the frame. Same parade ground, gate, field gun, stables and trough in dry daylight. Draw the background drill squads bareheaded with Kerala topknots in white coats and red sashes, no tricorn hats, to match the rest of the page. Keep the upper sky clear for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The two men face each other at arm's length, and Nagoji's profile holds Duarte's eyes. Nagoji: curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, coat, waistcoat and chain. Duarte: grey, lined, ink-stained clasped hands, closed black collar, no tab. The setting matches. Minor: a brown leather belt over the waistcoat is not in the costume spec. Balloon space is moderate: a thin sky band across the top above both heads, plus sky and low-detail roof tiles at the upper right.

Acceptable. Nagoji walks away with his back to Duarte toward the drilling lines, in white coat, red waistcoat, boots, topknot and grey temples, with the moustache visible in partial profile. Duarte stands bowed in the foreground with ink-stained hands, cross and closed black collar. A secretary hurries to his side. The open sky in the upper middle gives ample room for both captions. Minor: the secretary wears a white kurta with a shoulder cloth instead of the long brown coat and record book from earlier pages, and he is drawn large rather than small. The chain of office hangs diagonally across Nagoji's back like a baldric. Duarte's face sits in the upper quarter rather than the middle half of the height, but the frame is already 3:1, so no crop is expected.

Minor only. The Prince's training tunic here is sleeveless, while 21.2 and 21.4 show a long-sleeved wrap tunic. The background firing line is a little odd, with targets set between the firers. Nagoji is on model: curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. The two Nair guards stand behind the Prince with hands at their hilts. Open sky at top left and top centre holds all three lettering areas.

Clean. This is a bust shot rather than a very tight close-up, but the flat, set expression reads well. He matches 21.1 and 21.4 (face, forehead mark, topknot, white tunic) on the same red-dust drill ground. Open sky at upper left and upper right gives room for the balloon.

Acceptable. Varma is shown as a full back with hair and an ear rather than just a shoulder, but he stays faceless, unbandaged and in white silk with a gold border. The shielding arm ends in an ambiguous rounded elbow in front of the boy. The knife hand comes in from the stain edge with no owner shown. There is no blood and no priest. The gopuram, brass oil lamps and soft memory-stain edges are correct. Pale sky and the stain margin at top centre hold the caption.

Minor. Nagoji's coat sleeves are rolled back. Besides the correct brand and scar on the left forearm, an extra faint white scar line shows on his right forearm. The bible puts the scar only on the inner LEFT forearm. His face is fully on model, with clean chin, flush stud, grey temples and topknot. The Prince's long-sleeved training tunic matches 21.2. The two-shot staging is squared up. A wide band of sky at top centre holds both balloons.

v01 dresses the Prince in the white uniform coat with a red waistcoat and brass buttons. The bible reserves that coat for page 26. On this page he wears a plain training tunic, as in 21.1, 21.2 and 21.4. The beat is also unclear: the two Nair guards from 21.1 (bare arms, white cloth, red sashes, hands at sword hilts) are not identifiable. Nagoji glances only vaguely toward the drilling sepoys rather than past the Prince at his guards.
decisions.correction: The Prince must NOT wear any coat, waistcoat or buttons. He wears only his plain white long-sleeved wrap training tunic tied with a white cloth sash at the waist, sleeves rolled to the forearm, and plain white trousers, exactly as in the previous panel. He has no silks, jewels, chain or red cloth. Place the Prince in the middle ground, half-turned, with his face in three-quarter view. A few paces behind him, near the gate in the armoury wall, clearly show his TWO Nair guards. They are bare-armed men with moustaches and topknots, in white cloth crossed over the chest, red waist sashes and sheathed swords held at the hip, hands near the hilts, standing alert. Nagoji stands in the foreground left, three-quarter to camera, his eyes and head clearly directed over the Prince's shoulder at those two guards, not at the Prince or the firing line. Keep everything else that worked: Nagoji's face, curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold ear stud, grey temples and topknot; his white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain; the red-dust drill ground below the laterite bastion with the red conch flag; morning light; and the open blue sky across the upper third, left clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the old guard has a turban and a full grey beard with a topknot showing above the turban, while the escort on page 21.1 were bare-armed Nair guards with topknots and no turbans (22.2 matches this panel, so the page is consistent with itself). One small background musketeer at the far right stands roughly in line with a neighbour's muzzle. Prince matches 21.1 (topknot, forehead mark, plain white wrap tunic with sash). No painted text. Sky and the plain wall face give clear space at the top for both balloons.

Minor: three guards walk to the gate where the script implies two, and they are turbaned, matching 22.1 but not 21.1. The Prince is in the same plain white tunic as 22.1 and looks back over his shoulder with a set jaw. The open sky at upper right is clear for the balloon.

The Prince is dressed as a small copy of Nagoji's uniform: white coat with brass buttons, red waistcoat, red cuffs, breeches and riding boots. This breaks the chapter MUST MATCH line (a plain training tunic, no coat until page 26) and the neighbouring panels 22.1, 22.2 and 22.4, which all show the tunic. The catch also does not read as 'barely': he grips the wooden sword in a firm two-handed guard pointed at Nagoji, which could read as a thrust. Nagoji himself is correct: profile, flush gold stud, clean chin, grey temples, forearm scar, and his arm thrown out.
decisions.correction: The Prince must wear the same plain training clothes as in the neighbouring panels: a loose plain white cotton tunic with sleeves rolled to the forearm, tied at the waist with a plain cloth sash, a plain white lower garment, barefoot or in plain sandals. Give him NO coat, NO red waistcoat, NO brass buttons, NO red cuffs and NO riding boots: the white coat and red waistcoat belong to Nagoji alone. Show the catch as only just made: the plain brown wooden practice sword (all wood, no metal) arrives tumbling against the Prince's chest, and he clutches it awkwardly flat against his chest with both forearms, off balance, one foot stepping back, eyes wide. He is not in a ready guard and the sword does not point at Nagoji. Keep everything else that worked: Nagoji in uniform at left in profile, his arm still extended from the toss, the tiny flush gold stud, grey temples, clean-shaven chin, the drill ground with the conch flag, and the open sky in the upper left and centre left clear for the balloon.

decisions.issues: In all three beats Nagoji's ear has a stud with a small gold drop or bead hanging below the lobe. The author has ruled out any hanging drop and asked for this to be enforced in selection. Secondary: the legs in beat 1 are a confusing tangle of three boots, and the Prince wears European riding boots and breeches, unlike the plain training dress in 22.1 and 22.2. decisions.correction: Nagoji's ear ornament in all three beats must be one tiny flush gold stud sitting on the earlobe with NOTHING hanging from it: no drop, bead, pendant or ring below the lobe. decisions.issues: The script beat is wrong. Nagoji is crouched in the dirt with a drawn steel sabre, copying the Prince's pose, when he should be standing and watching. Ramayyan also crouches, so he does not read as having arrived silently at Nagoji's shoulder. The Prince holds a real steel sabre instead of the wooden practice sword. decisions.correction: Only the Prince is in motion. Ramayyan stands just behind Nagoji's shoulder, upright and still, having arrived without a sound, in plain white cloth with his palm-leaf bundle and stylus held at his chest. He does not crouch. Keep the 3:1 strip, the drill ground with the targets, field gun, gate and conch flag, the dust cloud of the roll, and the open sky band across the top left and centre clear for three balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only: Nagoji has a faint stubble shading on the jaw, though the chin reads clean-shaven with a flush gold stud, grey temples, topknot and the full uniform. Clean. The Rani matches her sheet (severe bun, plain white with a gold border, ear studs), and her hard gaze is turned right toward the drill line where her son trains. Clean. The Rani turns fully to face Nagoji. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a flush gold stud, grey temples and a topknot, and wears the white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. Minor only: a female spear-bearer at the far left wears a similar white sari and bun. She has a different, younger face and a red sash, so she reads as an attendant rather than a second Rani. Minor: the 'ghost of a smile' is very faint, closer to composed neutrality. The Rani matches her sheet: severe bun, small gold ear studs, white sari with a narrow gold border. The firing line is side-on with her behind it. The conch standard is plain. There is no text, and the open sky at upper right and centre takes both balloons.

The open hand holding the coin is Nagoji's RIGHT hand in both the main picture and the inset (thumb uppermost, the arm reaching from his forward side as he faces left). The script calls for his LEFT hand. The pale healed scar is painted on the inner RIGHT wrist and forearm, with a short crossing stroke that reads like a cross in the main picture. There is no thin scar across the palm. This contradicts the script and the bible, which places the brand and long white scar on the inner LEFT forearm. Everything else works: both faces match their sheets, Nagoji has the curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold stud, grey temples and topknot, the uniform and silver chain are correct, the coin moment and inset read clearly, and there is sky at upper left and centre for the balloons.
decisions.correction: Make the open hand Nagoji's LEFT hand in both the main picture and the inset. Keep the Senior Rani at left facing right and Nagoji at right facing her. Turn Nagoji slightly away from the camera into a three-quarter rear view over his left shoulder, his face in profile with the curled moustache and the flush gold ear stud visible, so that the arm reaching to her, nearest the camera, is his LEFT arm. His right arm stays down at his side. In the inset at lower right, his LEFT hand enters from the right edge in the white coat cuff with one plain brass button. It is palm up, fingers toward the left, thumb on the lower, near side of the hand, with the small worn gold coin resting in the palm and the fingernails ridged. The only scar is one thin pale healed line running across the palm. The wrist and forearm show no scars, lines, crosses or marks of any kind, and the cuff covers the wrist. Keep everything else as it is: the red-dust drill ground with the bastion and conch standard, both faces and costumes, the silver chain over the white coat and red waistcoat, and the open sky across the top of the frame for lettering.

decisions.issues: Minor: Nagoji holds out his right hand here. If the regenerated 24.2 uses his left hand, the coin changes hands between panels, but 24.3 does not specify a hand, so this is acceptable. The staging and room match 24.2: the Rani is at left, Nagoji at right, on the same drill ground. Both faces match their sheets. The hands are sound, there is no scar or text, and the large sky at upper left and centre takes both balloons.

Minor: this is a bust shot rather than a true face close-up, and her calm reads slightly stern, which suits the threat. Her face matches the sheet. Both firing lines are side-on with her behind them. The Prince wears Nagoji's full uniform: white European coat, red waistcoat and brass buttons. The Senior Rani, walking away, has gained a necklace, though she should wear no ornament. decisions.correction: The Prince wears a plain cream cotton training tunic, sweat-darkened, belted with a white cloth sash, over cream trousers and boots, as on the previous page. He has NO white coat, NO red waistcoat, no brass buttons and no jewels. The white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain belong to Nagoji alone in this panel. Both Nagoji and the Prince are STANDING on the open drill ground, with no crate, bench or seat. The Prince, about fourteen, beardless and narrow-shouldered with his small topknot, stands just at Nagoji's elbow, a head shorter. Both are turned toward the Senior Rani as she walks away. Keep the rest: the wide strip with Nagoji and the Prince at left and their faces in the middle band, Nagoji's curled moustache, clean chin, flush gold ear stud and grey temples. Keep the Senior Rani small at right walking away toward the gate, back straight, in her plain white sari with the narrow gold border and NO necklace or other ornament. Keep the laterite bastion, the conch standard and the open sky above for lettering.

decisions.issues: Only v01. The beat, mist, pre-dawn light and the Prince's smaller grey are right, and Nagoji is on model (curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, topknot, grey temples, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain). His MUST MATCH line, and pages 21 and 23 of the script, keep him in a plain training tunic until page 26, where 'the same white coat as the others' is the payoff. Kayal also shows a small white streak or star on her forehead, and she should have no white markings. decisions.correction: Keep this composition, mist, pre-dawn lavender sky, fort, torches, the red conch standard and both horses as drawn. Change only the Prince's clothes. He wears a plain knee-length cream cotton training tunic with no collar, no buttons, no braid and no coat or waistcoat, tied at the waist with a plain cream cloth sash, with loose cream trousers and plain dark riding boots. Nothing red is on him, and he has no silks or jewels. Only Nagoji wears the white European coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain. Kayal's face is solid bay with no white star, blaze or streak on the forehead. Keep the Prince's mount a smaller light dapple-grey with a darker grey mane, tail and lower legs, clearly shorter than Kayal.

decisions.issues: Only v01. The sunrise gold-and-green light, the trotting side by side and Nagoji's look are all good. Three things fail. First, the Prince rides a bay that is almost a copy of Kayal, but panel 25.1 puts him on a smaller grey. Second, he turns his head up and sideways toward Nagoji, while the script says he looks straight ahead, not at Nagoji. decisions.correction: Keep the sunrise over the tree line, the gold-and-green light, the drill ground, the fort and the clear sky in the upper part of the frame. The Prince rides a smaller light dapple-grey horse with a darker grey mane, tail and lower legs, clearly shorter than Nagoji's bay mare Kayal. His face is in three-quarter view, turned forward along his horse's line of travel, and his eyes look straight ahead between his horse's ears, never toward Nagoji. He wears a plain knee-length cream cotton training tunic with no collar, no buttons, no braid and no coat or waistcoat, tied with a plain cream cloth sash, with loose cream trousers and plain dark riding boots. Nothing red is on him. Only Nagoji wears the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain.

decisions.issues: Only v01. The beat is right: both men reined in with the horses facing each other, and there is a clear sky band for the three balloons. Nagoji is on model. Two things fail. The Prince's horse is a full-size bay, which breaks the smaller grey from 25.1. The Prince also wears Nagoji's white coat and red waistcoat instead of his plain training tunic, which the script holds back until page 26.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: both riders reined in, the two horses nose to nose facing each other, the fort wall and bastion behind, the morning light and the open sky across the top. The Prince's horse is a smaller light dapple-grey with a darker grey mane, tail and lower legs, a hand shorter than Nagoji's bay mare Kayal, so the two horses are told apart at a glance. The Prince wears a plain knee-length cream cotton training tunic with no collar, no buttons, no braid and no coat or waistcoat, tied with a plain cream cloth sash, with loose cream trousers and plain dark riding boots. Nothing red is on him. Only Nagoji wears the white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain.

decisions.issues: Only v01. The framing, low sun behind him, face, gold stud, topknot, grey temples and uniform are good, and the sky gives ample lettering space. There are two problems. On his bare left forearm the brand is drawn as a crisp dark circled glyph, like a stamp or tattoo with an arrow-like symbol inside. It reads as a sign or letter, when it should be a pale puckered patch of ridges blurred past reading. Second, the chin and jaw carry visible stubble texture, though he should be clean-shaven.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact framing, pose, expression, the low sun behind his head, the fort, the drill-ground background and the open sky above. His white coat sleeves come down to the wrists on both arms, with the red cuffs at the wrist, so both forearms are fully covered and no brand, scar, mark or symbol shows on any skin. Draw no circle, arrow, letter, stamp or tattoo-like mark anywhere on him. His chin, jaw and cheeks are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble hatching, and only the thick curled moustache is kept.

decisions.issues: Only v01. The wide strip, the gold light, the Prince's long look at Nagoji and Nagoji's likeness are good, and the sky has room for the balloons. Two things fail. The Prince's horse is a bay much like Kayal, though 25.1 puts him on a smaller grey. decisions.correction: Keep this wide composition with the two riders standing their horses in the gold early light, the Prince's face turned toward Nagoji in a long steady look, the fort wall and gate, and the open sky across the top. The Prince's horse is a smaller light dapple-grey with a darker grey mane, tail and lower legs, clearly shorter than Nagoji's bay mare Kayal. decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) is otherwise strong: the ash-striped Nair captain is muttering, Nagoji is in profile with a clean chin, ear stud and topknot, and the Prince in his white coat holds his water skin to the collapsed recruit. It fails on the brand. Nagoji's sleeves are pushed up, and the brand is on his RIGHT forearm, the one raised to his chin. It is drawn as a crisp dark circle with an X-like glyph inside, which reads as a legible symbol or cross. The bible asks for a blurred puckered patch on the inner LEFT forearm. The long scar is also on the right forearm, and a cross-shaped scar is painted on the left. The fort wall behind also has crenellated castle battlements, which do not match the plain parapets of the bastion panels.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition exactly as it is: the older, heavier Nair captain with ash stripes muttering at left, Nagoji in profile beside him with one hand at his chin, and behind them at right the Prince in his white coat holding his water skin to the lips of the collapsed recruit propped in the shade of the post. Fix only Nagoji's arms and the wall. His white coat sleeves come all the way down to the wrists with the cuffs closed, so no bare forearm skin shows on either arm. Draw no circle, stamp, symbol, cross, letter, scar or mark of any kind on his arms or hands; in this panel the brand and scar stay hidden under the left sleeve. The fort wall and angled bastion behind are plain red laterite with a low, plain, flat-topped parapet: no crenellations, merlons or castle-style battlements.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The pennant is a straight dark-blue saltire, not a diagonal crossed by a curved line, but it matches the rest of the page. There is light stubble shading on Nagoji's jaw, though his chin reads clean-shaven. Otherwise it is clean: evening on the laterite bastion, Nagoji in the white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain with a topknot, a gold stud and grey temples, and the Prince beside him in the same white coat with his forehead mark. The open sky across the top is good for the three balloons.

v01 (the only candidate) has the right framing: a close three-quarter-back view of the Prince at the parapet, looking out over the drill ground in evening light. The costume is wrong. He wears a loose white shirt with a cloth tied at the waist instead of the white European coat, red waistcoat and cravat he wears in 26.2, 26.4 and 26.5.
