decisions.correction: Keep the close three-quarter-back view of the Prince leaning his forearms on the red laterite parapet and looking out over the drill ground, not toward the viewer, with the gold evening light, the conch standard on the bastion and the open sky in the upper part of the frame. Change his costume to match the neighbouring panels on this page: a white European-cut coat with plain brass buttons and sleeves to the wrists, over a red waistcoat with a white cravat at the throat. He wears no loose shirt and no cloth tied at the waist. Keep his topknot and the white vertical marks on his forehead. On the drill ground below, show only a few small men in the same white coats, or an almost empty ground at day's end. Draw no torches or braziers burning on the bastion.

decisions.issues: In v01 (the only candidate) the scripted action is given to the wrong man. The Prince stands with his hands behind his back and does not roll his shoulders. Nagoji makes the panel's only physical gesture: he grips his bared left forearm, with the scar showing. Nagoji is also grinning with his eyes half-closed while he speaks a serious line, and there is noticeable stubble on his chin and jaw. The Prince has lost the forehead mark he has in 26.2. The two-shot, the evening bastion setting and the Prince's small smile all work.
decisions.correction: The action belongs to the Prince. He stands at Nagoji's side on the parapet walk in his white coat and red waistcoat, both shoulders visibly lifted and rolled back as in a drill exercise, chest open and arms loose at his sides. He glances up at Nagoji with a small, wry, lopsided smile, and keeps the white vertical marks on his forehead and his topknot. Nagoji stands still and level beside him, one hand resting on the parapet and the other at his side. His coat sleeves come down to the wrists, so no forearm skin, brand or scar shows. He does not grip, rub or roll up his arm. His expression is calm and steady, not grinning, and his chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble. Keep the two-shot framing, the gold evening light, the bastion with the red conch standard, and the open sky in the upper part of the frame for the balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The memory stain at the right edge is soft-edged but fairly opaque rather than faint. The Prince has no forehead mark here. Nagoji's face sits in the upper quarter of the strip. Otherwise the beat is clear: the Prince walks down the bastion steps in the same white coat and red waistcoat, the turbaned guards smile and nod rather than bow, and Nagoji watches from above with a clean chin, gold stud and silver chain. The boy of ten in white stands wide-eyed in a Kerala house courtyard at the edge. The open evening sky across the top centre takes both captions without touching faces.

Minor only. Thoma is clean-chinned with a moustache, but 27.3, 27.5 and the page 28 frames give him a short black beard. The bible has no beard rule for him, so this is a consistency note, not a failure. His betel stain is light (reddish lower teeth). Caption space is the sky strip across the top (about x 0.40 to 0.78, y 0 to 0.11). It fits two medium captions above the heads. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch24 uniform row: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat and chain over the coat.

Thoma grins with bright WHITE teeth, which fails his MUST MATCH (teeth stained dark red-brown with betel). He is also off-model against the neighbouring panels: a long grey-streaked beard and greying long hair tied back with a teal tint, so he reads as an older, different man from 27.1, 27.5 and page 28. Composition, hand on the gun, setting and sky space are otherwise good.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Thoma Ittyerah as the only named figure in the fort artillery yard, broad and grinning, one big hand flat on the bronze barrel and the other on his hip. Keep the tiled shed at left, the laterite walls, the crew at their places and open sky across the top for two speech balloons. Fix his teeth: where they show in the grin they must be visibly stained dark red-brown with betel, never white. Draw Thoma to match the neighbouring panels: shoulder-length curly BLACK hair worn loose, no grey in hair or beard, a thick black moustache and a short trimmed black beard, a small dark wooden cross on a cord, and a plain white cloth tunic with a white waist sash. No long or greying beard, no hair tied back, no blue or teal tint in the hair.

decisions.issues: The roles are reversed. Nagoji is the one bent over the gun, squinting along it and adjusting a brass quadrant. Thoma stands behind him pointing. Script 27.3 has THOMA squinting along the barrel and adjusting the elevation while Nagoji watches and speaks. Thoma's long greying-black beard also differs from 27.1 and 27.5. Nagoji's own look (topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin, stud, uniform) is correct.
decisions.correction: Thoma must do the aiming, not Nagoji. Turn the bronze field gun so it points away from the viewer, into the depth of the yard toward the distant wooden targets. Thoma Ittyerah crouches low at the breech, right of centre, cheek close to the metal, one eye shut, squinting along the barrel. Both his big hands push the wooden elevation wedge (quoin) under the breech. Draw him with shoulder-length curly black hair, a thick black moustache, a short trimmed black beard, a plain white cloth tunic with a white sash and a small wooden cross on a cord. Nagoji stands upright on the left, a step or two away, NOT touching the gun or any instrument, hands clasped behind his back, watching Thoma. He wears the white European-cut coat with plain brass buttons, red waistcoat, silver chain of office over the coat, knee breeches and riding boots. He has a Kerala topknot with first grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a tiny flush gold ear stud. Do not draw a brass quadrant or any other instrument on the barrel. Keep the packed-earth yard, laterite walls, tiled shot shed, background crew in white, and open sky across the upper third for two speech balloons, with both heads below that sky.

decisions.issues: The firing beat is staged wrongly. At the moment of discharge a crewman is bent over the breech with both hands on the gun, right in its recoil, which is the opposite of the 'fixed places, exact ritual order' drill the caption celebrates. The slow-match man is several paces away pointing his lit linstock into the air, so nobody is shown firing the gun. Thoma is clean-chinned, unlike 27.5 and page 28. The wide view, bursting target, smoke, setting and sky space are good.
decisions.correction: Keep the wide view of the artillery yard: laterite walls, the tiled shot shed at left, the bronze gun on its carriage firing with a burst of white smoke from the muzzle, the wooden target far downrange bursting into splinters, and open sky across the top for the caption. Fix the drill: at the moment of firing, no one touches or leans over the gun and no one stands behind the wheels or in the recoil path. The gunner stands beside the breech at arm's length, leaning away, touching the glowing slow match on his linstock to the vent. The rammer stands clear beside the muzzle with his rammer held upright. The loader stands clear on the other side holding the next round. Each man keeps a fixed drill spot. The gun may jump back slightly on its wheels. Thoma Ittyerah stands a few paces back watching, hands on hips. He has shoulder-length curly black hair, a thick black moustache and a short trimmed black beard, and wears a plain white cloth tunic with a white sash and a small wooden cross on a cord.

decisions.issues: Clean. Thoma grins through the smoke with visibly betel-stained red-brown and yellow teeth. His short black beard and curly black hair match page 28. Nagoji stands beside him in the white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain, with topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin and gold stud. Balloon space: smoky sky top centre (x 0.35 to 0.75, y 0 to 0.17) and clear sky top right (x 0.83 to 1.0) for Thoma's two balloons. Smoke over the wall between the heads (x 0.34 to 0.56, y 0.18 to 0.30) fits Nagoji's reply.

Minor: framed as a medium waist-up shot rather than a true close-up. Thoma's beard has grey streaks, and his betel staining shows only as yellowed teeth. The range targets have concentric rings but no lettering. The upper-right sky is clear for both balloons.

Clean. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch24 uniform row: curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, grey temples, topknot, silver chain, white coat, red waistcoat and buckled boots. Thoma's hand rests on Avraham's shoulder and he gestures toward Nagoji, who leans in a half bow. The sky across the top-left and centre is clear for three balloons. This panel's Avraham (black beard, soft black cap, brown frock coat with brass buttons) should be the reference look for the page.

It shows the script beat on the same dock as 28.2: Thoma laughs with betel-stained teeth and a hand on a barrel, and Avraham is unsmiling. The large upper-left sky is clear for lettering. Continuity flag, not a rejection reason because neither character has a sheet: Avraham's beard and hair are grey-streaked here but black in 28.2, and he wears a black robe-coat and pillbox cap instead of 28.2's brown buttoned frock coat and soft cap. Thoma's hair is long and tied back, with an earring and a cross pendant, while it is short in 28.2. The author may want a matching regeneration.

Nagoji's left coat sleeve is pushed up. His bare outer forearm, on the back-of-hand side, carries a crisp spoked-wheel emblem like a tattoo plus a scar line. That contradicts the bible: the brand belongs on the INNER left forearm as a pale puckered patch blurred past reading, and the script does not call for it here. Thoma has a moustache only, with no beard, unlike 28.1, 28.2, 28.3 and 28.5. Avraham has a brown beard and a beret-like cap, a third version of him on this page. A map with coastline lines stands in for the manifests. The ledgers show only faint, illegible line texture. The room, lamp, mat, cups and lighting are good.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, the single open-wick brass lamp lighting, the laterite walls and rafters, the woven mat, the brass cups and the three men seated cross-legged exactly as they are. Nagoji's unbuttoned white coat keeps BOTH sleeves down to the wrists with the cuffs at the wrists: no bare forearm skin shows on either arm, and there is NO mark, symbol, emblem, wheel, tattoo, brand or scar anywhere on his forearms or hands. Thoma Ittyerah has a full, short black beard joined to a thick moustache, with curly black hair, matching the dock panels on this page. Do not draw him with a moustache alone. Avraham ben Ephraim has a black chest-length beard, black curly hair, a soft black cap and a dark brown frock coat with a single column of brass buttons. Between them lie only closed or open account ledgers and loose cargo manifests whose pages are plain or faintly ruled, with no map, no coastline drawings, no writing, no numerals and no symbols.

decisions.issues: Minor: the brass oil lamp inside the boat's canopy has a faint teardrop outline round its flame that could read as a glass chimney, but it is tiny at print size. De Lannoy and Nagoji both match their sheets and the ch24 rows (clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain; De Lannoy's worn, patched, frayed coat). The curved talwar is lifted and weighed. Balloon space: the laterite wall at top centre and the sky at upper right.

The only candidate (v01) misses the script beat and breaks prop continuity. The script asks for a TIGHT shot on the hands, but this is a waist-up two-shot. The sword has become a short, straight European-style blade, while 29.1 shows a long curved talwar, the dialogue is about curving steel and 30.1 has the talwar in Nagoji's hand. decisions.correction: Frame this as a TIGHT close-up of the hand-over only, cropped from just above the two wrists to just below the sword, with no faces in frame. The sword is the SAME long talwar from the previous panel: a clearly curved, single-edged blade many times the length of its grip, with a gilded brass hilt, disc pommel and knuckle guard, never straight and never short. It is held level and offered hilt first. Nagoji's brown hand comes in from the right, with visibly ridged, uneven fingernails, out of a white European coat cuff fastened with two plain round brass buttons. His fingers are closing around the black-wrapped grip just below the guard. De Lannoy's pale, freckled hand comes in from the left out of a frayed, much-mended white cuff with loose threads and a darned patch. His palm rests open and flat on the flat side of the curved blade near its middle, fingers not wrapped around the edge. Behind the hands, show only softly blurred laterite wall and the dark timber of a spear rack in warm lamplight, with no door, yard, sky or flag. Keep the upper third of the frame plain, dark laterite wall for the balloon.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the blurred troops in the yard wear round brimmed hats, white coats and trousers, which reads slightly European rather than Travancore mundu (small background). De Lannoy leans arms-crossed against the spear rack with a sidelong gaze, as scripted. Nagoji matches his ch24 row (clean chin, stud, topknot, grey temples, uniform, silver chain). The room and lamp are consistent with 29.1. Balloon space: the laterite wall at top centre and the spear tips at top left.

Minor only: one drilling soldier wears a reddish turban. There is a plain timber shade frame in the yard, with no rope or noose. De Lannoy is on model (patched elbow, frayed cuffs, black-ribboned pale hair, no hat) and stands straightening in profile, looking out of the door at the men drilling. Both balloons fit in the sunset sky framed by the door, clear of his face.

Minor only: the sky through the door has gone from sunset to deep dusk, with torches lit (a plausible progression). The lamp's shadow falls loosely; the long shadows on the wall come more from the spears than clearly from De Lannoy. He is on model: the back view shows both patched elbows, the frayed cuffs and the black ribbon, and he turns his head back over his shoulder toward the off-panel Nagoji. The room matches the earlier panels. Balloon space: the plain laterite wall left of his head, or the top band.

Minor only. The yard seen through the door has a grey, European-looking crenellated stone wall that does not match the red laterite bastion in 30.3. The doorway sky is deep blue dusk with torches lit, which is darker than the later sunset in 30.3. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, grey temples, topknot, silver chain over the white coat, red waistcoat and plain brass buttons, with the talwar in his hands. De Lannoy has pale hair tied back and a patched, frayed coat, and his hand is on his chin. There is a brass open-wick lamp and no text. There is clear laterite wall for balloons at upper left (x 0.08-0.23, y 0-0.2) and upper right (x 0.66-0.74, y 0-0.25).

Minor only. It is the same armoury, but mirrored: the door is now on the left and the lamp on the right. A small plain white flag over a grey crenellated wall shows through the door; it is not the red conch standard and could read as a white flag. The beat is right: De Lannoy smiles at Nagoji, who still holds the talwar. Both principals match their sheets (clean chin, gold stud, chain over the coat; the coat is patched and frayed). There is no text. There is room for 3 balloons: the doorway sky (x 0.01-0.16, y 0.07-0.23) and the wall between the two heads (x 0.40-0.57, y 0-0.3).

Minor only. On the pennant the dark blue lines read close to a saltire with a small hook, a little different from the diagonal-plus-curve in 30.4. The sea and setting sun are more prominent than 'a distant line'. Otherwise right: De Lannoy is taller and bare-headed with pale hair; Nagoji has the topknot, the silver chain over the white coat and buckled boots. Both walk along the laterite parapet. Below, Maravar horse and musketeers in white coats drill, and a gun crew works a cannon. The red conch standard is shown, there is no text, and the hands are sound. There is open sky for the two captions (x 0.42-0.62 and x 0.75-1.0, y 0-0.16).

Minor only. The view is from roughly bastion level rather than strictly from below the staff. It matches the beat: there are no figures; the red standard with a silver conch is at the top, with the white pennant below it, crossed by a dark blue diagonal and a curved line; both lift against a sunset with the sun on the horizon. The laterite bastion and steps match 30.3. There is no text, and there is clear sky beside and below the pennant (x 0.6-0.95, y 0.3-0.56) for both captions.
